question: A custom tool renders a chart image from time-series data, and a downstream part of the agent's workflow needs the exact numeric data points as structured fields rather than parsed out of a text description. How should the tool handler return this?
options: A) Return the chart as an image block and repeat the data points again as a second text block
B) Return the data points inside a resource block's blob field alongside the rendered chart
C) Return the chart as an image content block and include the raw data points in structuredContent
D) Return only a text content block that lists the data points formatted as a comma-separated string
correct_answers: C) Return the chart as an image content block and include the raw data points in structuredContent
explanations: Text blocks are dropped when structuredContent is present since they are assumed to duplicate it, and repeating data as an extra text block does not provide the same reliable machine-readable access.
The resource blob field is meant for binary content addressed by URI, such as generated files; it is not the mechanism for returning exact numeric fields as structured data.

Correct: structuredContent is a separate JSON field on the result meant for machine-readable data; combined with an image block for the chart, this gives Claude both the visual and exact numeric fields.
A comma-separated text block requires Claude to parse the string to recover exact values, which is the pattern structuredContent exists to avoid for reliable machine-readable data.
